old: A hind might as well lay
new: A doe might as well lay
reason: A consequential consistency edit outside the ten flagged Books. At 17.10 Telemachus repeats Menelaus's lion simile from 4.27, and Homer repeats the lines (4.333–340 ≈ 17.124–131). B04-05 renders the animal 'doe' at 4.27 because 'hind' is unfamiliar and the simile turns on it, so the repeat uses the same word. Butler's 17.10 has no other 'doe' or 'deer'.
